_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Score a chart for Stale Winners...

description: Use this when the user wants app ideas or weak incumbents on a top chart, such as "which popular apps on the top free chart are badly rated or abandoned?". Pass the chart inputs and min_score. Scans all 100 chart apps and returns each with a Stale Winner score (0 to 100, 75 or more is high), its reasons, flags (low_rating, stale) and a download and revenue estimate range. Scores rank opportunities; they do not prove a market.

chart.description: Which top chart: free (default) or paid. grossing answers source_off: no allowed source publishes it.

country.description: Two-letter store country, such as us, gb or jp. Default us.

genre.description: Omit for the overall chart. A genre answers source_off: no allowed source publishes genre charts.

limit.description: How many rows to return, 1 to 100. Default 25. The whole chart is always scanned.

min_score.description: Only apps scoring at least this much. 75 or more is a high opportunity. Default 0.

store.description: apple (App Store, default). play answers source_off: Google Play charts load only through a path its robots.txt disallows.

name: app_tracker_opportunities

as_of.description: ISO 8601 time the data was published by its source or fetched from it. A cached answer keeps the time of its fetch.

source.description: Who the data comes from, to cite and to check it against.

stale.description: Present only when Apple's feed failed and the newest stored copy of the chart, up to 3 days old, was served instead. fetchedAt is that copy's time.

title: Score a chart for Stale Winners
